lessons.title: Salesforce: CTI Adapter and SCC-AC
lessons.why: Voice stays on Connect. The question is which system owns the digital channels and the case.
paras: The CTI Adapter is a managed package plus a serverless application that embeds the CCP in Salesforce. Install it in a sandbox first. Salesforce Contact Center with Amazon Connect goes further: telephony and in-app voice stay native to Connect, and messaging can be either platform's. The org needs Service Cloud Voice, and digital features need Digital Engagement.
Screen pop uses the attributes you stored and the ANI or the customer id. If you transfer to a phone number, Salesforce on the far side will not see those attributes.
points: One system of record for the case.
The serverless app has an IAM role. Review it.
Test outbound click-to-dial. It uses the caller ID rules.
lessons.mistake: Embedding the CCP and also running a second softphone.

lessons.title: ServiceNow Voice
lessons.why: ServiceNow can own assignment while Connect owns the conversation, if you map the queues on purpose.
paras: The ServiceNow document describes importing contact flows, optional Advanced Work Assignment routing, hold audio no longer than 5 seconds, and transfer-to-agent and transfer-to-queue flows. Queues in Connect get matching AWA queues. AI voice agents, if you bought them, plug into the inbound flow through a flow module.
Oauth and Lambda setup is part of the guide. That Lambda is subject to the same 8-second contract as any other.
points: A 5-second hold file is a hard constraint in that guide. Do not upload a 30-second loop and wonder.
Map queues by name in a table you review.
The placeholder phone channel is not a real number.
Test transfer flows. They are shared with ITSM in the guide's description.
lessons.mistake: Turning on AWA and Connect routing and letting both choose an agent.

lessons.title: Teams is a chat client in the published pattern
lessons.why: The AWS blog's Teams integration is not a SIP trunk into Teams Phone.
paras: A Teams app talks to Azure Bot Service, which calls API Gateway and Lambda, which starts a Connect chat and stores metadata in DynamoDB. Entra ID issues the token. Replies go back through the bot framework. That is chat.

If a Teams Phone user must receive a voice transfer, use Transfer to phone number to a number Teams Phone actually answers. Attributes will not cross. Screen pop has to be rebuilt on the Teams side or avoided.
points: Do not describe this blog as 'Connect telephony inside Teams'.
The Lambda is yours to secure.
Typing indicators and session lookup are application code.
Voice and chat are different projects. Staff them separately.
lessons.mistake: Buying a Session Border Controller because someone said Teams.

flow.label: Voice
flow.detail: A phone-number transfer, if you must.

lessons.title: CUCM and Webex beside Connect
lessons.why: There is no AWS-managed CUCM CTI adapter in the docs this campus cites. The seam is the phone number.
paras: Leave extensions on CUCM or Webex Calling. Claim or port the public contact-center numbers to Connect. When a Connect agent must reach a desk, transfer to that number. When a desk must reach the center, dial the Connect number. Webex Contact Center, if you still have it, is a second CCaaS during dual-run, not a component.

E911 for people who still have a CUCM phone can stay on CUCM. Agents who only have the CCP need the Connect E911 design in the Ecosystem track. Do not assume the PBX location covers a home agent on the CCP.
points: Test the transfer in both directions.
Codec and DTMF on the CUCM side still matter after the transfer.
Caller ID from Connect must be a number CUCM's route plan accepts.
Document which system records the second leg.
lessons.mistake: A diagram with a SIP trunk and no evidence Connect can register to it.

diagram.caption: They meet when one dials the other.
